_comment: Guided tour for FRC resolution in the emtk window. Targets are the spec's attr names and the windows and buttons the window draws; steps that need the user to act wait (await) and never press anything. The help page carries the long form.

steps.title: What this image resolves, not what the microscope could
steps.text: Fourier ring correlation splits your acquisition into two independent halves, correlates them ring by ring in frequency space and reports the frequency at which they stop agreeing. Above it the halves hold different noise and nothing else: it is the finest detail the data support, photon budget, drift and label included.

steps.title: Load the acquisition
steps.text: A frame stack, or a photon stream that will be binned into one. FRC needs many frames: the split must leave enough photons in each half to form an image. Choosing a file reads its channels; it does not measure.

await.hint: Press Browse (or drop a file, or type a path and press Enter) and choose the acquisition.

steps.title: The split IS the measurement
steps.text: The halves must be independent measurements of the same object. Even / odd frames is the default. Two channels means two detectors that saw the same structure, not two labels on different structures: those correlate nowhere and the tool reports the field of view as the resolution. That failure gives a number, not an error.

steps.title: The criterion travels with the number
steps.text: Fixed 1/7 is the usual convention for fluorescence images; half-bit and 2 sigma depend on the image size, and on the same data the three disagree by tens of per cent. Quote which one you used. Set the pixel size too: without it the answer is in pixels.

steps.title: Measure
steps.text: The two halves are formed and correlated in the background; the status line reports the resolution.

await.hint: Press Measure and wait for the status line.

steps.title: Read the crossing, and know what no crossing means
steps.text: The resolution is where the correlation drops through the threshold (the marker). No crossing is a real answer: either the halves agree at every frequency the sampling can show, or they agree nowhere (too few photons, or a split whose halves were not independent). The Help button has the rest.
